newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS -- Prominent businessman Peter Woo issued a statement expressing his decision to run for the post of the future Hong Kong chief executive.

-- China has decided not to hold any international functions in the next five years and not to apply to host international competitions in the next 10 years in order to save resources and concentrate on the economy.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Peter Woo and Tung Chee-hwa were both born in Shanghai, educated in the West, and succeeded shipping tycoons. They both ran big businesses and had extensive international connections. But Woo was positive and straightforward, resembling Western politicians, while Tung was more careful and traditional.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS -- A battered wife and her two young daughters were forced to sleep on the streets for a week. The one-year-old daughter was suffering from skin infection.
-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng warned Japanese right-wing groups that there would be no good results hurting the feelings of Chinese people.
-- Chinese Premier Li Peng listed Chinese economic achievements, saying that inflation was under control.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Under many favourable economic factors, Hong Kong's stock exchange might be able to challenge historical records. Analysts said China might further decrease the interest rates.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- China's top representative in Hong Kong acknowledged improved Sino-UK relations and noted cooperation had also spread to Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp.
-- Chief Secretary Anson Chan said she hoped the post-handover administration would continue to publish reports on its work.

--The Bank of China put the ghost of last year's cancelled HK$5 billion note issue behind it following the huge response to its latest HK$2 billion money raising venture which attracted HK$9 billion in subscriptions.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- China's pharmaceutical industry would invest 100 million yuan in development during the next five years, part of which would be raised by offering shares to foreign investors in up to five pharmaceutical companies.

-- People's Bank of China chairman Wang Xuebing said China was making progress in efforts to cool inflation, open its foreign exchange market and maintain growth as state-owned companies work off their huge debt loads.
